lessons.title: Rehearse and choose one change
lessons.goal: I can try our story and choose one change.
success: I can rehearse my own part.
I can choose one cue or pose to change.
I can keep my choice in my arts log.
words: Try your part before the show.
A sign to start or change.
What a watcher saw or heard.

artist_cards.work: The den with a clear cue
artist_cards.description: The group point to a wide space. Their hands move close to show a small space. The director waits until all are ready, then points to the word Start. The group show a small den. Each still pose lasts three comfortable seconds.
artist_cards.prompt: How does the cue help the group?
artist_cards.model_answer: The director checks that all are ready. One clear cue helps the group change pose together.

artist_cards.work: The den with a clear end
artist_cards.description: The group try the same three parts. A watcher cannot see the last pose. The group turn their hands towards the watcher and try again. The watcher sees a small roof. The story order stays the same.
artist_cards.prompt: How could we check our end pose?
artist_cards.model_answer: They changed the way the last pose faced. Ask a watcher what they see, then use their real words to check the change.

staff_guidance.plain_language: Resilience can include pausing, asking for help, changing a plan and trying a manageable next step. It does not mean hiding feelings, tolerating harm or continuing through pain.
staff_guidance.scope: Both pathways work at Explore. The optional GROW next level stretch adds evidence for later review. This is rehearsal and refinement; next week is performance and review. These lessons do not complete or certify the award.
staff_guidance.art_specialist_help: Model one small change, then let pupils decide whether it helps. Keep the story order steady so the comparison is fair. Look for each pupil's own role, choice, trial and response to real feedback, rather than a polished show.
staff_guidance.sensory_and_emotional_access: Use invented situations and role labels. Offer actor, seated performer, silent performer or director. No forced speech, public performance, eye contact, personal account or touch. Agree a calm space, stop cue and return cue. A rehearsal may be shared privately with a trusted member of staff.
staff_guidance.safety: Keep a clear personal space. Walk only; no running, lifting, falls, climbing, throws or contact. Props and scenery are imagined. Use an agreed open-hand stop cue. A freeze lasts at most three comfortable seconds, with normal breathing, then relax. Seated and hand-only versions are equal options.
prompt_ladder: Point to the instruction or place.
Model the first step only, then return the task.

adaptations.cognition_and_learning: Keep three BUILD parts or four GROW beats visible in a book or cue note. Rehearse once before changing one thing. Read one feedback point, model the first step only, then return the choice to the learner.
adaptations.communication_and_interaction: Use short cue words or point to a cue word. Reserve the open hand for Stop. Offer pointing, signing, a seated gesture, silent acting, directing or an adult scribe. Give processing time. Use We changed ... because ... .
adaptations.semh: Use the familiar invented scene when available and offer an honest fresh route. Agree roles and audience privately. A pause, smaller movement, role change or private staff rehearsal is valid. Do not measure confidence or require disclosure.
adaptations.sensory_and_physical: Use a chair or hands only. Agree safe space and a quiet cue. Keep voices at talking level. No touch or surprise sounds. A still pose lasts only up to three comfortable seconds while breathing normally.
adaptations.eal: Plan in any language. Link each cue word to a gesture. Allow oral rehearsal before a short log. Check meaning, sequence and the learner's intended change rather than accent or spelling.

misconceptions.claim: Refine means change the whole story
misconceptions.correction: Keep the three story parts. Test one cue or pose.

misconceptions.claim: A rehearsal must work first time
misconceptions.correction: A trial can show what needs another try. Keep the real result.

misconceptions.claim: Only a speaking actor has a role
misconceptions.correction: Acting seated, silent movement and directing can each include a real creative choice.

staff_guidance.careers_line: Performers, directors and stage teams use cues, agree roles, rehearse safely and respond to feedback.
staff_guidance.audience: Audience is the class and invited staff only. Agree who will watch before sharing. No public audience, family audience, outside guests or online publication is planned. Pupils may choose a private staff rehearsal and an accessible role for next week.

cold_call.foundation: Which part will we try again?
cold_call.middle: What one thing did we change?
cold_call.higher: What did the watcher see that helps us judge the change?

ta_focus.I do: Point to the part being tested. Name the single change. Ask what the pupil notices before giving an explanation.
ta_focus.We do: Invite one real choice from each learner. Model the first step only and return control. Keep the chosen cue accessible.
ta_focus.Independent: Record the learner's actual role, trial and words. Confirm the watcher's comment. Do not turn a group outcome or adult model into evidence of every pupil's contribution.

lessons.artist_use_note: Both comparison groups and stories are invented original classroom examples. They illustrate rehearsal choices and are not an external arts encounter or pupil work. No published dialogue is reproduced.
lessons.evidence: Keep the available earlier plan with its original date, a new dated rehearsal note, the actual feedback and each learner's confirmed choice and reason. Show the part before and after a change when possible. Record support and any unfinished work honestly. Fresh work is dated today. A photograph or recording is optional under local consent procedures and is not needed.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find our story plan if it is here.
Choose act, sit, stay silent or direct.
Keep your own clear space.
Use the open-hand stop cue.
stages.say: We will rehearse The new den. You can keep or change your role. If the old plan is missing, we make a fresh three-part plan today. Our audience is the class and invited staff only, and you can rehearse with a staff member privately.
stages.good: Each learner has a safe role and an available plan or a fresh route.
stages.fallback: Read the three parts aloud: want a den, space too small, choose a small den. Let the pupil point or direct one hand pose.
stages.answer: A role may be acting, a seated pose, silent movement or directing. A missing old plan stays missing; date today's new work today.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: First: We want a den.
Next: The space is small.
Last: We choose a small den.
Show the part you will do.
stages.say: Use your real story from last week if it is here. This three-part den story is our fresh route if needed. Tell me which part you chose. You do not need to tell a story from your life.
stages.good: Pupils identify their actual contribution and recover a workable order.
stages.fallback: Offer first, next or last, then show the chosen part seated.
stages.answer: The new den is an invented story. The order is want a den, find the space too small, choose a smaller plan.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch the same story twice.
First, I rush the last cue.
Next, I wait until all are ready.
I change just one thing.
Which cue is clear?
stages.say: In our first adult model, I give the last cue too soon. Then I try the same three parts again. I wait until the performers are ready before the last cue. I keep each freeze to three comfortable seconds and breathe as usual. The watcher says which version they could follow. This is a model, not your evidence.
stages.good: Adult contrasts two trials with a single change in cue timing and uses a concrete watcher question.
stages.fallback: Use three hand poses from a chair. Ask the pupil to point to the cue that gives time to get ready.
stages.answer: A cue after checking readiness can help the group change together. Check: What did I change? If the pupil names a different feature, repeat only the last transition slowly.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Try our three parts once.
A watcher says: I saw ___.
Choose one cue or pose to change.
Try that part again.
Keep it or try once more.
stages.say: We will do the story once before deciding. The watcher names a part they saw or could not yet see. We pick one change, such as waiting for the cue or turning the last pose. Let each pupil make a real choice. If the order is still unclear, rehearse first, next and last before adding a change.
stages.good: The group bases one manageable target on a real trial and each pupil contributes or confirms a decision.
stages.fallback: Adult is the watcher and models only the first part; pupils direct the next cue or choose between two poses.
stages.answer: If the watcher can name the first and last parts, test one feature. If not, return to the three-part order. This is the hinge decision; do not pile on several targets.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Rehearse your part with the group.
Keep first, next and last.
Test one change in a cue or pose.
Ask a watcher what they saw.
In your book or arts log, keep your own choice.
stages.say: Use the real plan or the fresh den story. Rehearse once, choose a cue or pose change, then try again. A director can choose when the cue comes; a seated or silent performer can choose a clear hand shape. The watcher is a class member or invited staff member. Keep the real comment, even if the change does not help yet.
stages.good: Each learner makes or directs an actual rehearsal contribution, tests one change and records a confirmed choice.
stages.fallback: Use a staff-only seated trial. The pupil directs the adult with a point to the next cue word; record the instruction actually given.
stages.answer: Example only: I waited for the group before my cue. The watcher saw us end together. A pupil may instead discover that the cue needs another try; that is useful evidence too.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Tell a watcher what you changed.
Watcher: I saw ___.
Choose one thing to keep.
Relax and store your plan.
stages.say: Ask the maker whether the comment matches their aim. Use the last two minutes to relax, reset chairs and store the plan and feedback for tomorrow. The record should say what actually happened, not that the show is finished.
stages.good: Learner confirms actual feedback and identifies one feature to keep or revisit.
stages.fallback: Staff member reads back the pupil's choice and the witnessed response. The pupil can correct either.
stages.answer: A useful comment names a cue, pose or clear story part. Good acting alone does not tell the maker what helped.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: My role was ___.
I tried changing ___.
The watcher saw ___.
Next time I will ___.
stages.say: Date the rehearsal today. I can write your words, read them back and let you change them. Keep the real target for tomorrow. If we did not finish a trial, say that and plan the next step.
stages.good: Dated log separates the actual role, tested change, response and next step.
stages.fallback: Offer cue or pose as a choice and scribe the confirmed words.
stages.answer: Example only: I tried a slow cue. The watcher saw the last pose. Tomorrow I will check we all wait for the cue.

Supported: Use the three den story parts.
Choose a role with the adult.
Pick one cue or pose to change.
Try it with help.
Point to your own choice for your log.
Independent: Rehearse the three parts in order.
Ask a watcher what they saw.
Choose and test one change.
Keep the feedback and your own part.
Say what to try next.
Aspire: Try two ways to give one cue.
Ask which helps the group most.

log: I will keep or change ___ because ___.

Keep the three story parts. Test one cue or pose.
A rehearsal must work first time
A trial can show what needs another try. Keep the real result.
Only a speaking actor has a role
Acting seated, silent movement and directing can each include a real creative choice.
kit: For three or four pupils: books or arts logs and pencils.
Available three-part story plan and real feedback from last week, if present.
Clear personal spaces or chairs for hand poses. All props and the den are imagined.
Keep today's choice and actual watcher comment for the next lesson. No device or costume is needed.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Show wide hands, close hands and a small roof. Say: First, next, last.
15 to 30 seconds
Give the last cue before the model is ready. Say: That cue was too soon.
30 to 45 seconds
Repeat. Check readiness and give one calm cue. Hold at most three comfortable seconds.
45 to 60 seconds
Ask: Which ending could you follow? Keep the watcher's actual reply and name the one change.
models: Teacher model only: I changed when I gave the last cue. I waited until the group were ready. The watcher could see the small den at the end.
Teacher model only: The watcher still missed the last part. I will try turning my last pose towards them next time.
lessons.cover: Recover the real three-part story if available. Otherwise read the fresh den story in Starter and date the new work today. Model one cue change. Pupils rehearse, use a class or staff watcher's actual comment and test one cue or pose. Keep individual choices and feedback for tomorrow. Use the seven-stage 40-minute timings, accessible roles and the three-second comfortable freeze limit.

lessons.title: Refine our story for the show
lessons.goal: I can use a real comment to make one part clear.
success: I can rehearse the three parts.
I can test one change from a real comment.
I can name my role and next step for the show.
words: Try your part before the show.
Set to start when the cue comes.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find our plan and real watcher note.
Choose your role again.
A fresh trial is fine if work is missing.
Use clear space and the stop cue.
stages.say: Yesterday's real note can help us choose today's target. If it is missing or we were absent, we make a new short trial and get feedback today. You can act, work seated, stay silent or direct. We will agree an accessible role for next week.
stages.good: Learner has a genuine target source or a fresh route; no attendance or feedback is assumed.
stages.fallback: Use the den story and a seated staff-watched rehearsal. Record today's contribution only.
stages.answer: A fresh watcher comment is valid. Never guess yesterday's words or backdate a record.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Read or hear one real comment.
What did the watcher see?
Pick one part to try again.
Say: We can change ___.
stages.say: Read only a comment that was actually made. A note such as I could not see the end points to a clear target. The group still chooses what to change. We can turn the end pose towards the watcher, then test it.
stages.good: Pupil links one actual comment to a manageable rehearsal target.
stages.fallback: Give two choices after reading the real note: change the cue, or turn the pose. Let the pupil choose.
stages.answer: If the viewer missed the ending, a clearer final pose may help. If no comment exists, do the short baseline trial now.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch the end pose face away.
A watcher says what they see.
I turn the pose towards them.
I try it again and ask once more.
I keep the story order.
stages.say: I show the small-roof ending facing away. I ask the watcher what they could see and use their actual reply. I turn the same pose towards them, without moving closer, then try again. A still pose lasts at most three comfortable seconds with normal breathing. I ask whether the roof is now clear.
stages.good: Adult models a feedback-led change and checks its effect without changing the entire story.
stages.fallback: Show the hand pose seated. Pupil directs the angle with a point; adult does not reposition the pupil's body.
stages.answer: The changed feature is facing. Ask: What stayed the same? The roof pose and story order stay the same. If unclear, show the two endings once more.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Agree one change from our real note.
Rehearse it once.
The watcher says what is clear.
Keep the change or try again.
Agree our start and stop cues.
stages.say: Use the chosen target and rehearse the full three parts. Invite a learner to give the cue. If a watcher still cannot follow first and last, return to those parts slowly. Keep the real response and do not call every trial a success.
stages.good: Group tests a feedback-led target and agrees cues that every role can use.
stages.fallback: Adult supports the first cue, then returns the next cue or pose decision to the learner.
stages.answer: If the watcher follows the start and end, keep the useful change and check cues. If not, revisit one transition rather than adding new dialogue. This is the hinge decision.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Rehearse the story with your change.
Keep your own role and safe space.
Ask one watcher what they see now.
Agree your role and cue for next week.
In your arts log, keep the change and next step.
stages.say: Use the real den sequence or a fresh three-part version. Try the chosen change and gather one specific response. Next week the audience is the class and invited staff only. Agree a speaking, seated, silent or directing role; a private staff rehearsal remains available. Do not promise or record a performance that has not happened.
stages.good: Each learner refines a real contribution, checks feedback and has a provisional accessible role and cue for next week.
stages.fallback: Pupil directs a seated adult trial and chooses a cue or angle. Record the creative decision and agreed future role without claiming future performance.
stages.answer: Example only: We turned the last pose so the watcher saw the small den. I will give the start cue next week. If a role is undecided, record that and agree a choice privately later.

stages.name: Review
pupil: What did our change help?
What still needs a try?
Check each person knows their cue.
Store the plan for next week.
stages.say: Read the learner's note back. Check role, cue and actual response separately. This is preparation for next week's performance and review. In the last two minutes, relax and store the plan and logs safely.
stages.good: Group knows what to keep, what remains unfinished and how each learner can take part next week.
stages.fallback: Use a quiet one-to-one check: point to role, point to start cue, confirm next step.
stages.answer: A ready plan states the three parts, roles and cues. It does not prove that the future show or review has already happened.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: The real comment was ___.
We changed ___.
It helped or needs more work because ___.
My role and cue next time are ___.
stages.say: Keep your own words about the rehearsal today. I can scribe and read them back. Record a real next step. We have rehearsed and refined; we will perform and review next week.
stages.good: Log records actual feedback, tested revision, its effect and a future role or next decision.
stages.fallback: Scribe a short confirmed phrase. A gesture can show which pose changed.
stages.answer: Example only: The viewer missed the roof. I turned my hands. They saw it then. Next time I will wait for the final cue.

Supported: Hear one real watcher note.
Pick a cue or pose to change.
Try the story with the adult.
Choose your role and cue for next time.
Point to what changed for your log.
Independent: Use real feedback to choose one change.
Rehearse and check what the watcher sees.
Keep or change the tested feature.
Agree your role and cues for next week.
Log your own part and next step.
Aspire: Compare the first and later trial.
Say how one change helped the viewer.
Choose one small check before the show.

log: The watcher saw ___ after the change.
This helped or needs more work because ___.
My role and cue for next time are ___.

The makers choose one useful change and test it.
Rehearsing now proves we performed next week
Date today's rehearsal today. Keep next week's performance as a plan.
Ready means every pupil must speak
Agree acting, seated, silent or directing roles with clear cues.
kit: For three or four pupils: books or arts logs and pencils.
Available story plan and actual feedback from Monday; use a fresh trial if they are missing.
Clear personal spaces or chairs for hand poses. All props and the den are imagined.
Keep the final rehearsal plan, accessible roles, cues and individual logs for next week.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Show a small roof pose facing away. Ask what the watcher can see.
15 to 30 seconds
Use the actual reply. Say: I will turn the pose towards you.
30 to 45 seconds
Repeat the same end pose facing the watcher. Freeze for at most three comfortable seconds.
45 to 60 seconds
Ask what is clear now. Say: I keep this change if it helps. Next week is the show.
models: Teacher model only: The watcher said the end was hard to see. I turned my roof pose. The watcher saw the small den. Next week I will wait for the last cue.
Teacher model only: We still need to practise the end cue. Our next step is to try that part once before the show.
lessons.cover: Use the real Monday feedback when present. If absent, give the den story a fresh baseline trial and ask a class or staff watcher for one comment. Model changing the facing of a pose. Pupils rehearse one revision, check its effect and agree accessible roles and cues for next week. Keep performance and review as future actions. Follow the 40-minute timings and safe three-second freeze limit.

lessons.title: Rehearse the group story
lessons.outcome: Rehearse and refine the group performance.
lessons.goal: I can rehearse our scene and choose one clear target.
success: I can play or direct my agreed role.
I can use a real trial to choose one change.
I can log my own choice and the viewer's response.
words: Practise a scene before the show.
The move from one story beat to the next.
One thing we choose to improve.

artist_cards.work: The small show with a cue keeper
artist_cards.description: A group rehearse plan, change, choice and result. The first cue comes before everyone is ready. In the next trial, a cue keeper checks each role, points to the word Start, then starts. The group begin the new small move together.
artist_cards.notice: Which part changes in the second trial?
artist_cards.prompt: How can we test whether a cue helps?
artist_cards.model_answer: The cue keeper checks readiness before giving the cue. Keep the same scene and ask a viewer whether the chosen move begins together.

artist_cards.work: A pause that shows a choice
artist_cards.description: A group show wide moves, a smaller space, a choice and a new small move. A viewer misses the choice. The group add a quiet pause before asking What could we try? The viewer now notices that the group make a new plan.
artist_cards.notice: What did the viewer miss at first?
artist_cards.prompt: How might a pause make our choice beat clear?
artist_cards.model_answer: The viewer missed the choice. A pause separates the change from the response. We need our own real trial before claiming it helps our performance.

misconceptions.correction: Record each learner's actual role, decision and help separately.

staff_guidance.careers_line: Performers, directors and stage teams use cues, agree roles, rehearse safely and respond to feedback.
staff_guidance.audience: Audience is the class and invited staff only. Agree who will watch before sharing. No public audience, family audience, outside guests or online publication is planned. Pupils may choose a private staff rehearsal and an accessible role for next week.

cold_call.foundation: Which part will we try again?
cold_call.middle: What one thing did we change?
cold_call.higher: What did the watcher see that helps us judge the change?

ta_focus.I do: Point to the part being tested. Name the single change. Ask what the pupil notices before giving an explanation.
ta_focus.We do: Invite one real choice from each learner. Model the first step only and return control. Keep the chosen cue accessible.
ta_focus.Independent: Record the learner's actual role, trial and words. Confirm the watcher's comment. Do not turn a group outcome or adult model into evidence of every pupil's contribution.

lessons.artist_use_note: Both comparison groups and stories are invented original classroom examples. They illustrate rehearsal choices and are not an external arts encounter or pupil work. No published dialogue is reproduced.
lessons.evidence: Keep the available earlier plan with its original date, a new dated rehearsal note, the actual feedback and each learner's confirmed choice and reason. Show the part before and after a change when possible. Record support and any unfinished work honestly. Fresh work is dated today. A photograph or recording is optional under local consent procedures and is not needed.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find our scene plan if it is here.
Choose an actor, seated, silent or director role.
Keep your own clear space.
Use the agreed stop cue.
stages.say: Use the scene about a smaller show space from last week when available. Missing plans or missed sessions do not become invented evidence. The fresh route is four beats: a wide show, a smaller space, a new choice, a small show. Agree an accessible role and audience.
stages.good: Each learner has a real source plan or fresh route and a voluntary accessible role.
stages.fallback: Read the four fresh beats aloud and let the learner direct a seated hand version.
stages.answer: A new scene or trial is dated today. Existing records keep their original date. No one needs to explain a personal change.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Recall plan, change, choice and result.
What is your own part?
Which part needs a clearer cue?
Keep any real feedback from last week.
stages.say: Ask each learner to point to or state their actual contribution. Read a genuine earlier comment if available; otherwise observe a short trial today. Our story is invented, and every role can make a creative choice.
stages.good: Learner identifies a personal contribution and the group recovers the four-beat order.
stages.fallback: Offer one beat at a time. Use a labelled sketch or gesture instead of a spoken account.
stages.answer: The choice beat shows the group asking or testing an idea. The result shows their new small move working. If those are mixed up, rehearse just those two.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch two trials of one transition.
First, the cue comes before all are ready.
Next, the director checks and gives one cue.
The story stays the same.
What does the viewer see now?
stages.say: I use the invented cue-keeper example. The scene keeps the same four beats. First I rush the cue into the small move. Then I check the roles and give one calm cue. Ask a real viewer whether the change begins together. Do not script their answer. We can keep or reject a change after the trial.
stages.good: Adult isolates a transition target and models testing it against real audience understanding.
stages.fallback: Use two seated hand roles and let a pupil point when the next cue should come.
stages.answer: The target is cue timing, not a new plot. Check: Which feature changed, and what stayed the same? Repeat the transition if pupils cannot separate the two.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Run our four beats once.
Ask: Which part was hard to follow?
Choose one target as a group.
Try that part again.
Keep the viewer's real comment.
stages.say: Run a baseline before choosing a target. Each pupil can offer an idea by speaking, pointing or directing. Choose one manageable feature: cue, pause, voice or move. If the viewer cannot identify the change and response, simplify those two beats before adding detail.
stages.good: The group agrees one target from an actual trial and records how learners took part in the choice.
stages.fallback: Use two options linked to the real comment. Adult models the first beat only, then pupils give the next cue.
stages.answer: If the viewer names the smaller space and new small move, refine one feature. If not, return to the four-beat sequence. This is the hinge decision.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Rehearse a short scene of about 30 to 60 seconds.
Keep plan, change, choice and result.
Test one target in a second trial.
Ask a class or staff viewer what they saw.
In your arts log, keep your own part and the result.
stages.say: Use the previous invented scene or the fresh four-beat route. Keep both trials short and comparable. Each learner makes or directs a real choice. Ask one agreed viewer from the class or invited staff. Use the actual response to decide what to keep. If a trial is unfinished, record that honestly.
stages.good: Each learner has a witnessed contribution, a specific tested target and a pupil-confirmed record of the outcome.
stages.fallback: Rehearse seated with hands or let the pupil direct staff through the four beats. A private staff-only trial is valid.
stages.answer: Example only: I waited for all roles before my cue. The viewer saw the small move begin together. A viewer may still miss the choice; keep that honest result as the next target.

stages.name: Review
pupil: What did the viewer understand?
Which change will we keep?
What still needs a try?
Store the plan and notes for Wednesday.
stages.say: Separate the maker's aim from what the viewer saw. The group can disagree with a suggestion and give a reason. In the last two minutes, relax, reset the space and keep the current outline with the genuine rehearsal note.
stages.good: Group chooses a supported next action and every learner can confirm their own record.
stages.fallback: Read a short real viewer phrase and ask keep, change or try again.
stages.answer: A useful decision links the feature to the viewer response. A general claim that it was better needs a detail.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: My role and choice were ___.
Our target was ___.
We tried ___, then ___.
The viewer noticed ___.
Next time I will ___.
stages.say: Record today's date, your actual part, the target and the real response. An adult can scribe and read your words back. This rehearsal is progress towards next week's performance; it does not close the award.
stages.good: Log records individual contribution and support alongside the group trial and keeps future actions separate.
stages.fallback: Ask one question at a time and confirm the learner's response before recording.
stages.answer: Example only: Our target was the choice beat. I added a pause. The viewer saw us think before the new move. Next I will check the end cue.

Supported: Use the four-beat story with staff help.
Choose a role and one feature to test.
Try the scene twice in a safe way.
Ask a viewer what they saw.
Confirm your own choice for the log.
Independent: Run the four-beat scene once.
Choose one target from a real response.
Rehearse with one change.
Check the viewer's understanding.
Log your part, choice and next step.
Aspire: Complete the same scene and log.
Compare the first and later trial.
Link one feature to what the viewer saw.
Choose a clear check for the next rehearsal.

log: The target from our real trial was ___.
First we tried ___. Next we tried ___.
We will keep or change ___ because ___.
misconceptions: Refinement needs a new story
Keep the four-beat scene. Compare one feature across two short trials.
A viewer's response must match our aim
Keep what the viewer really saw. Use a mismatch as information for the next trial.
Group success proves everyone made every choice
Record each learner's actual role, decision and help separately.
kit: For up to five pupils: available arts logs, books and pencils.
The real four-beat outline and feedback from last week, where available.
Clear personal spaces or chairs for silent hand performance. All props and scenery are imagined.
Keep today's target, actual feedback and individual contributions for Wednesday. No device or costume is required.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Name plan, change, choice and result. Show the transition into the small move.
15 to 30 seconds
Give a cue too soon in the adult model. Ask which part was hard to follow.
30 to 45 seconds
Repeat the same transition after checking readiness, then give one calm cue.
45 to 60 seconds
Ask what the viewer saw. Name cue timing as the only planned change and retain the actual reply.
models: Teacher model only: I directed the cue into the result. I waited until each role was ready. The viewer saw the new small move start together.
Teacher model only: The viewer still missed our choice. I will try a pause before What could we try? in the next rehearsal.
lessons.cover: Recover last week's invented smaller-space scene and real notes if available. Otherwise use the four fresh beats in Arrival and date the new trial today. Run a baseline, choose one target, model a single cue change and rehearse a comparable second trial. Collect a real class or staff viewer response and each learner's contribution. Keep the outline for Wednesday. Follow the seven-stage 40-minute timing and accessible safety rules.

stretch.label: Optional next level stretch
stretch.task: Choose one skill in your role. Compare your first and later trial. What changed? What did the viewer see? Set one small skill goal for Wednesday.
stretch.evidence: Keep your own choice, both real trial notes and the viewer's words. Add your skill goal and how you will check it.
stretch.why_optional: This adds reflection for a possible later level review. It is optional and does not alter the Explore task or certify the award.
stretch.good: Learner uses a concrete difference between real trials to justify a manageable personal practice goal.
stretch.fallback: Staff ask the same short questions and scribe confirmed words. A directed or seated trial can provide the real comparison.

lessons.title: Refine the scene for next week
lessons.outcome: Rehearse and refine the group performance.
lessons.goal: I can use real feedback to refine the scene and plan my role.
success: I can test one change from real feedback.
I can explain how the change affects the viewer.
I can agree my role, cue and next step for the show.
words: What a viewer saw and their useful comment.
A sign that tells a role when to act.
The people who watch the performance.

artist_cards.work: The small show with a cue keeper
artist_cards.description: A group rehearse plan, change, choice and result. The first cue comes before everyone is ready. In the next trial, a cue keeper checks each role, points to the word Start, then starts. The group begin the new small move together.
artist_cards.notice: Which part changes in the second trial?
artist_cards.prompt: How can we test whether a cue helps?
artist_cards.model_answer: The cue keeper checks readiness before giving the cue. Keep the same scene and ask a viewer whether the chosen move begins together.

artist_cards.work: A pause that shows a choice
artist_cards.description: A group show wide moves, a smaller space, a choice and a new small move. A viewer misses the choice. The group add a quiet pause before asking What could we try? The viewer now notices that the group make a new plan.
artist_cards.notice: What did the viewer miss at first?
artist_cards.prompt: How might a pause make our choice beat clear?
artist_cards.model_answer: The viewer missed the choice. A pause separates the change from the response. We need our own real trial before claiming it helps our performance.

staff_guidance.plain_language: Resilience can include pausing, asking for help, changing a plan and trying a manageable next step. It does not mean hiding feelings, tolerating harm or continuing through pain.
staff_guidance.scope: Both pathways work at Explore. The optional GROW next level stretch adds evidence for later review. This is rehearsal and refinement; next week is performance and review. These lessons do not complete or certify the award.
staff_guidance.art_specialist_help: Model one small change, then let pupils decide whether it helps. Keep the story order steady so the comparison is fair. Look for each pupil's own role, choice, trial and response to real feedback, rather than a polished show.
staff_guidance.sensory_and_emotional_access: Use invented situations and role labels. Offer actor, seated performer, silent performer or director. No forced speech, public performance, eye contact, personal account or touch. Agree a calm space, stop cue and return cue. A rehearsal may be shared privately with a trusted member of staff.
staff_guidance.safety: Keep a clear personal space. Walk only; no running, lifting, falls, climbing, throws or contact. Props and scenery are imagined. Use an agreed open-hand stop cue. A freeze lasts at most three comfortable seconds, with normal breathing, then relax. Seated and hand-only versions are equal options.
prompt_ladder: Point to the instruction or place.
Model the first step only, then return the task.

adaptations.cognition_and_learning: Keep three BUILD parts or four GROW beats visible in a book or cue note. Rehearse once before changing one thing. Read one feedback point, model the first step only, then return the choice to the learner.
adaptations.communication_and_interaction: Use short cue words or point to a cue word. Reserve the open hand for Stop. Offer pointing, signing, a seated gesture, silent acting, directing or an adult scribe. Give processing time. Use We changed ... because ... .
adaptations.semh: Use the familiar invented scene when available and offer an honest fresh route. Agree roles and audience privately. A pause, smaller movement, role change or private staff rehearsal is valid. Do not measure confidence or require disclosure.
adaptations.sensory_and_physical: Use a chair or hands only. Agree safe space and a quiet cue. Keep voices at talking level. No touch or surprise sounds. A still pose lasts only up to three comfortable seconds while breathing normally.
adaptations.eal: Plan in any language. Link each cue word to a gesture. Allow oral rehearsal before a short log. Check meaning, sequence and the learner's intended change rather than accent or spelling.

misconceptions.claim: A rehearsal plan proves the performance is done
misconceptions.correction: Record the rehearsal today and the performance only after it happens next week.

misconceptions.claim: A refined scene must be longer or louder
misconceptions.correction: A pause, silent cue or smaller clear move may make the same scene easier to follow.

misconceptions.claim: The audience must include families or outside guests
misconceptions.correction: The planned audience is the class and invited staff only. Agree accessible roles and private staff rehearsal options.

staff_guidance.audience: Audience is the class and invited staff only. Agree who will watch before sharing. No public audience, family audience, outside guests or online publication is planned. Pupils may choose a private staff rehearsal and an accessible role for next week.

cold_call.foundation: Which part will we try again?
cold_call.middle: What one thing did we change?
cold_call.higher: What did the watcher see that helps us judge the change?

ta_focus.I do: Point to the part being tested. Name the single change. Ask what the pupil notices before giving an explanation.
ta_focus.We do: Invite one real choice from each learner. Model the first step only and return control. Keep the chosen cue accessible.
ta_focus.Independent: Record the learner's actual role, trial and words. Confirm the watcher's comment. Do not turn a group outcome or adult model into evidence of every pupil's contribution.

lessons.evidence: Keep the available earlier plan with its original date, a new dated rehearsal note, the actual feedback and each learner's confirmed choice and reason. Show the part before and after a change when possible. Record support and any unfinished work honestly. Fresh work is dated today. A photograph or recording is optional under local consent procedures and is not needed.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find our scene and Monday's real target.
Choose your role and audience again.
Use seated, silent or directed work if needed.
Keep clear space and the stop cue.
stages.say: Recheck roles and audience. A pupil may change to seated, silent or directing work, or rehearse privately with staff. Our only planned audience is the class and invited staff. If Monday's work is missing, make a fresh short trial before choosing a target.
stages.good: Learner confirms an accessible role and genuine evidence source; missing work has an honest fresh route.
stages.fallback: Use the four-beat smaller-space story and a staff-only seated trial.
stages.answer: A role or audience agreement can change. Record today's actual choices and do not invent earlier feedback.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Read or hear one real viewer comment.
Which beat does it help us check?
Choose one change to test.
Keep the four story beats.
stages.say: Use one specific comment from Monday or today's baseline. A viewer may say the choice was hard to see. The makers then decide what to test, such as a pause before What could we try? Ask each learner for a contribution to the decision.
stages.good: Target follows actual feedback and relates to a named story beat.
stages.fallback: Read a single confirmed phrase and offer cue or pause as two possible changes.
stages.answer: Feedback gives information. The group retains creative ownership and tests the proposed change rather than assuming it will work.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch the choice beat twice.
First, the small move starts at once.
Next, I pause and ask: What could we try?
The same story stays in order.
What does the viewer see now?
stages.say: I show the same invented choice beat twice. In the first adult model, the new move follows at once. Next I pause, ask What could we try? at talking level and give the cue. A still pose lasts at most three comfortable seconds with normal breathing. I ask a real viewer whether the decision is easier to follow.
stages.good: Adult models a small feedback-led revision and checks the audience interpretation directly.
stages.fallback: Use a silent seated version: pause, show two small hand choices, point to one, then repeat it.
stages.answer: The pause can separate the change from the choice. It does not prove success on its own. Check the viewer's actual reading; if still unclear, simplify to two gestures.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Agree one change from the real comment.
Rehearse the scene once.
Ask what the viewer understood.
Keep it, change it or try again.
Check each role has a clear cue.
stages.say: Run the four beats with the agreed target. Ask the viewer to name the problem and the response. If they can, check how each cue works. If not, return to the unclear beat with a smaller gesture or short line before running again.
stages.good: Group uses actual feedback to judge a revision and agrees accessible transitions for each role.
stages.fallback: Staff cue only the first beat. Pupils choose or direct the following cues and can answer by pointing.
stages.answer: If the viewer identifies the smaller space and the new plan, retain useful detail. If not, simplify the choice/result link. This is the hinge decision.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Rehearse a short scene of about 30 to 60 seconds.
Use one agreed change and safe cues.
Ask a class or staff viewer what they saw.
Agree your own role and cue for next week.
In your arts log, keep real feedback and your next step.
stages.say: Use the established scene or the fresh four-beat route. Try the revision, ask for one specific response, then make a reasoned decision. Agree a provisional running order: ready check, start cue, scene, end cue and relax. Next week is performance then review, for the class and invited staff only. No public or family audience is planned. Keep an accessible role and staff-only alternative.
stages.good: Each learner tests an actual refinement and records a real contribution. The group has a workable next-week plan with clear role and cue agreements.
stages.fallback: Use a short private staff rehearsal. A learner can direct one transition or choose a silent cue; record that action and agree a suitable future role.
stages.answer: Example only: We added a pause before the new plan. The viewer saw the choice. I will give the end cue next week. If that cue is not settled, keep it as a next decision rather than a completed agreement.

stages.name: Review
pupil: What helped the viewer follow the scene?
What still needs a short practice?
Check roles, start cue and end cue.
Store the plan for next week.
stages.say: Read back each learner's part, real response and next step. Confirm how to pause or stop. The plan is for next week; it is not a record of a performance already given. In the last two minutes, relax and store all notes with the outline.
stages.good: Learners confirm accurate rehearsal evidence and an accessible preparation plan.
stages.fallback: Check role and cue one-to-one by gesture or short spoken choice.
stages.answer: A useful readiness check covers roles, order, cues, safe space and how to stop. It does not require a polished or public performance.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: My role and choice today were ___.
We used the real comment ___.
Our change helped or needs more work because ___.
My role, cue and next step for the show are ___.
stages.say: Date the note today and use your own words. Keep real feedback even when it differs from our aim. Next week we perform, then review what actually happens. We do not close the award in this rehearsal lesson.
stages.good: Dated log distinguishes actual refinement from future performance and preserves each learner's voice.
stages.fallback: Staff scribe one confirmed phrase at a time. Pupil confirms a role and one cue or next decision.
stages.answer: Example only: The viewer missed our choice. I directed a pause and they saw the new plan. Next week I will give the start cue after everyone is ready.

Supported: Use the four-beat story and one real comment.
Pick one cue or pause to refine.
Try it with staff help.
Agree an accessible role and cue for next week.
Confirm your own choice and next step.
Independent: Use actual feedback to choose a target.
Rehearse and check what the viewer understands.
Keep or change the tested feature for a reason.
Agree roles, cues and the safe running order.
Log your part and one next step.
Aspire: Complete the same rehearsal and plan.
Compare your aim with the viewer response.
Explain why you will keep or change one feature.
Set a small check before next week's performance.

log: My actual role and support today were ___.
This helped or still needs work because ___.
My role, cue and next step for next week are ___.
misconceptions: A rehearsal plan proves the performance is done
Record the rehearsal today and the performance only after it happens next week.
A refined scene must be longer or louder
A pause, silent cue or smaller clear move may make the same scene easier to follow.
The audience must include families or outside guests
The planned audience is the class and invited staff only. Agree accessible roles and private staff rehearsal options.
kit: For up to five pupils: available arts logs, books and pencils.
The current four-beat scene outline and actual Monday feedback, if available.
Clear personal spaces or chairs for silent hand performance. All props and scenery are imagined.
Keep the revised running order, accessible role and cue agreements, and each learner's actual rehearsal log for next week.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Show the choice beat without a pause, then ask what the viewer saw.
15 to 30 seconds
Repeat with a quiet pause and the original line What could we try?
30 to 45 seconds
Give one calm cue for the same small move. Keep personal space and normal breathing.
45 to 60 seconds
Ask what is clearer. Keep the actual reply and name one next check for the performance.
models: Teacher model only: I directed a pause before the group chose the small move. The viewer saw us make a new plan. Next week I will check readiness before the start cue.
Teacher model only: The viewer still could not see the result. We will practise the final small pose once before the show, rather than claiming it is finished.
lessons.cover: Use the current invented scene and genuine Monday feedback where present. Otherwise run a new four-beat baseline and record today's response. Model a pause before the choice, test one agreed revision and check the viewer's understanding. Agree accessible roles, cues, safe running order and one next check for next week's class-and-invited-staff performance and review. Do not claim it has already happened or close the award. Follow the 40-minute stages.

stretch.label: Optional next level stretch
stretch.task: Compare your aim with what the viewer saw. Will you keep or change one part? Say why. Set one skill to check before the show.
stretch.evidence: Keep your real trial note, your own reason and the viewer's words. Add a skill goal and a way to check it.
stretch.why_optional: This adds reflection for possible later level review. It is optional and does not certify the award or replace the coming performance and review.
stretch.good: Learner links a choice to actual trial evidence, makes a reasoned decision and plans a manageable personal skill check.
stretch.fallback: Staff ask the same short questions and scribe confirmed responses. Use a private seated or directed trial as the real evidence.

scope: Explore for both pathways. Optional GROW next level stretch retains additional evidence without changing core success criteria.
timing: Arrival 0-3; Starter 3-6; I do 6-12; We do 12-18; Create 18-32; Review 32-37; Exit 37-40 minutes.
